newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: PRESS DIGEST-Australian Sports News - May 20.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST-Australian Sports News - May 20.

text.p: (Compiled for Reuters by Media Monitors)
THE AUSTRALIAN

New South Wales won the Super League Tri-Series final against Queensland last night in extra time following a 22-all draw after 80 minutes. Noel Goldthorpe kicked the winning field goal in the 104th minute of the game, after a series of disallowed tries ad missed field goals in extra time. Page 22.

Soccer Australia chairman David Hill said yesterday minor premiers Sydney United and South Melbourne would be charged with bringing the game into disrepute and face expulsion from the national league following crowd disturbances at Sunday's preliminary fial at Parramatta Stadium. Fans clashed with each other and police when Croat-Greek ethnic tension flared after Sydney United's 1-0 victory. Page 22.

Hawthorn full-forward Jason Dunstall will know today if his Australian Football League career is over, after re-injuring his left knee in Sunday's loss to Carlton. He will be examined today by leading orthopaedic surgeon Dr Peter Wilson, and it is believed that if his knee requires a reconstruction, the team captain may retire. Page 22.
THE SYDNEY MORNING HERALD

Champion jockey Shane Dye almost collapsed with exhaustion after riding Cronus to victory in yesterday's Adelaide Cup at Morphettville. The win equalled Malcom Johnston's 1979-80 record of 35 metropolitan stakes wins. Page 43.

New South Wales second-rower Adam Muir was cleared last night to play in next week's Australian Rugby League State of Origin match after the ARL judiciary gave him the benefit of the doubt over a spear tackle charge. It was the second time Muir had faced the judiciary in four weeks. Page 44.

The Australian women's basketball team defeated Russia at Melbourne Park last night, making a clean sweep of the best-of-five Test Series. The Opals led 43-27 at half time and went on to win 81-62. Page 43.
THE AGE

The Australian Football League ruled out taking action against the Brisbane coach and two players after they appeared to dispute umpiring decisions after the siren in their five point loss to Fremantle. The umpires advised the League that coach John Northy, and players Michael Voss and Jason Akermanis, had not breached the laws of the game, and the matter was deemed closed. Page B8.

The Australian men's basketball team narrowly won the first game of its five-Test series against Croatia last night. The Boomers led for most of the match, but Croatia got to 76-71 with two minutes remaining. The final score was 82-73. Page B6.

Essendon's Michael Long and St Kilda's Peter Everitt are expected to meet today to try to resolve allegations that Everitt racially vilified Long in Sunday's match. Essendon manager Danny Corcoran said the Australian Football League was keen to keep the mtter confidential. Page B8.
THE HERALD SUN

The Australian Rugby Union said yesterday it would not put extra seats on the Melbourne Cricket Ground arena for the Bledisloe Cup Test in July, ending speculation that the ARU would try to achieve a world record attendance. The match is expected to attract almost 100,000 people, just short of the unofficial record of 104,000 set at Edinburgh's Murrayfield Stadium. Page 77.

Richmond defeated the West Coast Eagles 18.11 (119) to 9.13 (67) in front of a crowd of 26,721 at the Melbourne Cricket Ground last night. The Tigers set up the win with an eight-goal blitz in the second quarter, with forward Joel Bowden kicking four goal in 16 minutes. Page 80.

Queensland motorcycle world champion Michael Doohan reached equal-second on the list of all-time 500cc Grand Prix winners with yesterday's victory in the Italian Grand Prix, but conceded that Giacomo Agostini's record number of wins was probably out of his reach. The result took Doohan to 95 championship points, 17 ahead of Spaniard Alex Criville. Page 74.
THE DAILY TELEGRAPH

Australian junior swim coach Bill Sweetenham regards this week's Oceania Championships as "essential experience" for the future, rather than a campaign for medals and short-term glory. He said the primary goal was to ensure Australia's young swimmers were ready to make the transition from age ranks to open competition. Page 64.

The relationship between the New South Wales Rugby Union and the leading premiership clubs deteriorated yesterday when the ruling body banned 13 Super 12 players from playing in the AAMI Cup this weekend. The NSWRU listed the availability of Waratah playes based on medical assessments, but clubs say a number of the banned players wanted to compete this weekend. Page 63.

The Australian men's hockey team may be without captain Michael York and halfback Paul Gaudoin for the opening match of the six-Test series against Pakistan at the Perth Hockey Stadium tomorrow night. York, who has not played since March after suffering a hamstring strain, is considered doubtful, while Gaudoin is rated only a 50-50 chance. Olympian Brendan Garard is also out of action with a stress fracture of the foot. Page 65.
-- Reuters Sydney Newsroom 61-2 9373-1800
